context: Applied contracts 3.0.0-draft.3 and the merge-time fixes: scopeAuthorizes adopted, optional superseded.by, legacy post entry_type, new delivery reasons, exchangeStatus on the store API, RetrievalAnnex moved, correctionFor conflicts, gitignore, offline switch, calibration script, doc counts.
rationale: It was `corrections.find(...)`, so competing corrections were separated by array order — append order, ULID order, the producer's clock. That is an invented resolution (C22 INV-11): the store reported one of two equally-authorized statements as governing with nothing in the evidence to justify the choice. The two tie-breaks that ARE properties of the statements now apply first (higher class wins per ADR §4.3 rule 1; among equals the narrower scope wins, because a correction scoped src/auth/ is a narrower claim than one scoped src/), and genuine ties become conflicts: both corrections retained, both on rec.conflicts, status conflicted, currentUseClaim refusing, correctionFor returning nothing. Mutation-checked — restoring array order fails all three new tests. The c22 it.todo is removed and replaced by real tests including a reversed-delivery-order pair.
summary: correctionFor resolves by evidence class, then by scope specificity, and returns undefined when equal-class corrections share identical coverage; the reducer marks those records conflicted
